      # projects: ~165s. That is affordable per-PR, and it is the difference

name: CI - Affected

# ARCH-CI-005: Replaced global npm run scripts with nx affected commands
# SEC-CI-002: All third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs
# ARCH-CI-006: Removed github.sha from NX cache key
# ARCH-CI-007: Split lint/type-check/test into parallel jobs so build always runs
# ARCH-CI-008: Increased timeouts (cold cache), reduced parallel (memory), save Nx cache after build
# ARCH-CI-009: Push-to-main runs affected lint/type-check/test/build as code-health.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # The merge queue (main ruleset) builds each group's merge commit and asks
  # for the same required checks; a workflow that does not listen here
  # leaves every queued entry waiting until the queue's timeout.
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

# SEC-CI-021: Minimum token permissions — prevents compromised actions from
# pushing commits, creating releases, or modifying repository settings.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '22'
  NPM_CONFIG_CACHE: .npm-cache
  SENS_API_GATEWAY_CI_FEATURES: health,telemetry,metrics,strict-security,scada-display,lorawan,signed-deploy,tpm,st-bytecode,multi-task-scheduler,opc-ua-server,live-debug,license-enforce

jobs:
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      base_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
      dependency_audit_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.dependency_audit_required }}
      docs_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.docs_changed }}
      farm_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.farm_checks_required }}
      full_validation: ${{ steps.range.outputs.full_validation }}
      has_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.has_changes }}
      deploy_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.deploy_changes }}
      head_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
      infra_image_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_infra }}
      infra_matrix: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.infra_matrix }}
      is_pr: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}
      range_reason: ${{ steps.range.outputs.range_reason }}
      rust_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.rust_checks_required }}
      selection_reason: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.selection_reason }}
      sensor_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.sensor_checks_required }}
      validation_started_epoch: ${{ steps.range.outputs.validation_started_epoch }}
    steps:
      # SEC-CI-002: pinned to SHA
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Resolve immutable affected range
        id: range
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "validation_started_epoch=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if git ls-remote --exit-code --refs origin refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null; then
              git fetch --force --no-tags origin \
                '+refs/tags/deployed/development:refs/tags/deployed/development'
            else
              lookup_status=$?
              if [ "$lookup_status" -ne 2 ]; then
                echo "::error::Unable to resolve the development deployment baseline from origin."
                exit "$lookup_status"
              fi
              if git rev-parse --verify refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                git tag --delete deployed/development
              fi
            fi
          fi
          node scripts/ci/resolve-affected-range.ts \
            --event-name "${{ github.event_name }}" \
            --ref "${{ github.ref }}" \
            --pr-base-sha "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}" \
            --head-sha "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --development-ref deployed/development

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm

      - name: Install workspace graph dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --prefer-offline

      - name: Resolve Nx and catalog scope
        id: scope
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/ci/select-deployment-scope.ts \
            --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            --base-sha "$BASE_SHA" \
            --head-sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --requested-services auto \
            --channel development
      - id: check
        env:
          DEPLOY_CHANGES: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_images }}
          VALIDATION_REQUIRED: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.validation_required }}
        run: |
          echo "has_changes=$VALIDATION_REQUIRED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "deploy_changes=$DEPLOY_CHANGES" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shared setup: install + cache (reusable via needs + cache restore)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  install:
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Cache Nx
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .nx/cache
          key: nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit

      # Persist node_modules for downstream jobs
      - name: Cache node_modules
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: nm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lint, type-check, test: PR + push-to-main code-health gate
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  lint:
    needs: [install, detect-changes]
    if: >-
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true' &&
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' ||
       (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # continue-on-error removed: lint failures must block PR merge.
    # BEFORE: lint errors showed green in GitHub — no signal to reviewers or authors.

pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

# ARCH-CI-005: Replaced global npm run scripts with nx affected commands
# SEC-CI-002: All third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs
# ARCH-CI-006: Removed github.sha from NX cache key
# ARCH-CI-007: Split lint/type-check/test into parallel jobs so build always runs
# ARCH-CI-008: Increased timeouts (cold cache), reduced parallel (memory), save Nx cache after build
# ARCH-CI-009: Push-to-main runs affected lint/type-check/test/build as code-health.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # The merge queue (main ruleset) builds each group's merge commit and asks
  # for the same required checks; a workflow that does not listen here
  # leaves every queued entry waiting until the queue's timeout.
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

# SEC-CI-021: Minimum token permissions — prevents compromised actions from
# pushing commits, creating releases, or modifying repository settings.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '22'
  NPM_CONFIG_CACHE: .npm-cache
  SENS_API_GATEWAY_CI_FEATURES: health,telemetry,metrics,strict-security,scada-display,lorawan,signed-deploy,tpm,st-bytecode,multi-task-scheduler,opc-ua-server,live-debug,license-enforce

jobs:
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      base_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
      dependency_audit_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.dependency_audit_required }}
      docs_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.docs_changed }}
      farm_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.farm_checks_required }}
      full_validation: ${{ steps.range.outputs.full_validation }}
      has_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.has_changes }}
      deploy_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.deploy_changes }}
      head_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
      infra_image_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_infra }}
      infra_matrix: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.infra_matrix }}
      is_pr: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}
      range_reason: ${{ steps.range.outputs.range_reason }}
      rust_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.rust_checks_required }}
      selection_reason: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.selection_reason }}
      sensor_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.sensor_checks_required }}
      validation_started_epoch: ${{ steps.range.outputs.validation_started_epoch }}
    steps:
      # SEC-CI-002: pinned to SHA
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Resolve immutable affected range
        id: range
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "validation_started_epoch=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if git ls-remote --exit-code --refs origin refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null; then
              git fetch --force --no-tags origin \
                '+refs/tags/deployed/development:refs/tags/deployed/development'
            else
              lookup_status=$?
              if [ "$lookup_status" -ne 2 ]; then
                echo "::error::Unable to resolve the development deployment baseline from origin."
                exit "$lookup_status"
              fi
              if git rev-parse --verify refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                git tag --delete deployed/development
              fi
            fi
          fi
          node scripts/ci/resolve-affected-range.ts \
            --event-name "${{ github.event_name }}" \
            --ref "${{ github.ref }}" \
            --pr-base-sha "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}" \
            --head-sha "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --development-ref deployed/development

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm

      - name: Install workspace graph dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --prefer-offline

      - name: Resolve Nx and catalog scope
        id: scope
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/ci/select-deployment-scope.ts \
            --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            --base-sha "$BASE_SHA" \
            --head-sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --requested-services auto \
            --channel development
      - id: check
        env:
          DEPLOY_CHANGES: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_images }}
          VALIDATION_REQUIRED: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.validation_required }}
        run: |
          echo "has_changes=$VALIDATION_REQUIRED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "deploy_changes=$DEPLOY_CHANGES" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shared setup: install + cache (reusable via needs + cache restore)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  install:
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Cache Nx
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .nx/cache
          key: nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit

      # Persist node_modules for downstream jobs
      - name: Cache node_modules
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: nm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lint, type-check, test: PR + push-to-main code-health gate
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  lint:
    needs: [install, detect-changes]
    if: >-
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true' &&
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' ||
       (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # continue-on-error removed: lint failures must block PR merge.
    # BEFORE: lint errors showed green in GitHub — no signal to reviewers or authors.

      migration_required: ${{ needs.build-development-images.outputs.migration_required == 'true' }}
      image_prefix: ${{ needs.build-development-images.outputs.image_prefix }}
      selection_reason: ${{ needs.build-development-images.outputs.selection_reason }}
    secrets: inherit

  development-delivery-status:
    needs:
      - detect-changes
      - build-development-images
      - development-deploy-contract
      - development-deploy-mode
      - deploy-development
    if: >-
      always() &&
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.deploy_changes == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    steps:
      - name: Require successful development delivery
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          results=(
            "build-development-images:${{ needs.build-development-images.result }}"
            "development-deploy-contract:${{ needs.development-deploy-contract.result }}"
            "development-deploy-mode:${{ needs.development-deploy-mode.result }}"
          )
          # A valid operator hold is a declared state, not a failed delivery:
          # the images are built and pinned, only the droplet rollout waits.
          # Every other mode must have deployed.
          if [ "${{ needs.development-deploy-mode.outputs.mode }}" != 'held' ]; then
            results+=("deploy-development:${{ needs.deploy-development.result }}")
          fi
          for result in "${results[@]}"; do
            if [[ "$result" != *:success ]]; then
              echo "::error::Development delivery did not complete: ${result}"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

  development-timing-summary:
    needs:
      - detect-changes
      - build-development-images
      - deploy-development
    if: >-
      always() &&
      github.event_name == 'push' &&
      github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' &&
      needs.deploy-development.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    steps:
      - name: Publish development phase durations
        env:
          VALIDATION_STARTED_EPOCH: ${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.validation_started_epoch }}
          IMAGE_STARTED_EPOCH: ${{ needs.build-development-images.outputs.image_started_epoch }}
          IMAGE_FINISHED_EPOCH: ${{ needs.build-development-images.outputs.image_finished_epoch }}
          DEPLOY_STARTED_EPOCH: ${{ needs.deploy-development.outputs.deploy_started_epoch }}
          DEPLOY_FINISHED_EPOCH: ${{ needs.deploy-development.outputs.deploy_finished_epoch }}

name: CI - Affected

# ARCH-CI-005: Replaced global npm run scripts with nx affected commands
# SEC-CI-002: All third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs
# ARCH-CI-006: Removed github.sha from NX cache key
# ARCH-CI-007: Split lint/type-check/test into parallel jobs so build always runs
# ARCH-CI-008: Increased timeouts (cold cache), reduced parallel (memory), save Nx cache after build
# ARCH-CI-009: Push-to-main runs affected lint/type-check/test/build as code-health.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # The merge queue (main ruleset) builds each group's merge commit and asks
  # for the same required checks; a workflow that does not listen here
  # leaves every queued entry waiting until the queue's timeout.
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

# SEC-CI-021: Minimum token permissions — prevents compromised actions from
# pushing commits, creating releases, or modifying repository settings.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '22'
  NPM_CONFIG_CACHE: .npm-cache
  SENS_API_GATEWAY_CI_FEATURES: health,telemetry,metrics,strict-security,scada-display,lorawan,signed-deploy,tpm,st-bytecode,multi-task-scheduler,opc-ua-server,live-debug,license-enforce

jobs:
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      base_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
      dependency_audit_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.dependency_audit_required }}
      docs_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.docs_changed }}
      farm_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.farm_checks_required }}
      full_validation: ${{ steps.range.outputs.full_validation }}
      has_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.has_changes }}
      deploy_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.deploy_changes }}
      head_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
      infra_image_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_infra }}
      infra_matrix: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.infra_matrix }}
      is_pr: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}
      range_reason: ${{ steps.range.outputs.range_reason }}
      rust_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.rust_checks_required }}
      selection_reason: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.selection_reason }}
      sensor_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.sensor_checks_required }}
      validation_started_epoch: ${{ steps.range.outputs.validation_started_epoch }}
    steps:
      # SEC-CI-002: pinned to SHA
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Resolve immutable affected range
        id: range
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "validation_started_epoch=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if git ls-remote --exit-code --refs origin refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null; then
              git fetch --force --no-tags origin \
                '+refs/tags/deployed/development:refs/tags/deployed/development'
            else
              lookup_status=$?
              if [ "$lookup_status" -ne 2 ]; then
                echo "::error::Unable to resolve the development deployment baseline from origin."
                exit "$lookup_status"
              fi
              if git rev-parse --verify refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                git tag --delete deployed/development
              fi
            fi
          fi
          node scripts/ci/resolve-affected-range.ts \
            --event-name "${{ github.event_name }}" \
            --ref "${{ github.ref }}" \
            --pr-base-sha "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}" \
            --head-sha "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --development-ref deployed/development

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm

      - name: Install workspace graph dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --prefer-offline

      - name: Resolve Nx and catalog scope
        id: scope
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/ci/select-deployment-scope.ts \
            --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            --base-sha "$BASE_SHA" \
            --head-sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --requested-services auto \
            --channel development
      - id: check
        env:
          DEPLOY_CHANGES: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_images }}
          VALIDATION_REQUIRED: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.validation_required }}
        run: |
          echo "has_changes=$VALIDATION_REQUIRED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "deploy_changes=$DEPLOY_CHANGES" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shared setup: install + cache (reusable via needs + cache restore)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  install:
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Cache Nx
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .nx/cache
          key: nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit

      # Persist node_modules for downstream jobs
      - name: Cache node_modules
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: nm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lint, type-check, test: PR + push-to-main code-health gate
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  lint:
    needs: [install, detect-changes]
    if: >-
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true' &&
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' ||
       (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # continue-on-error removed: lint failures must block PR merge.
    # BEFORE: lint errors showed green in GitHub — no signal to reviewers or authors.

discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

      # FARM-MEDIUM-302 — this step used to open with

      # so nx exited 0 having run nothing. The line read like a gate and was
      # pure theatre; it is removed rather than left to reassure readers.
      #
      # What remains is real, but it only compiles the files a PR TOUCHES:
      # type-check-changed-files writes a temp tsconfig with
      # `files: [changed…], include: []`. A stale file nobody edited is
      # invisible to it — which is how a farm-service spec stayed uncompilable
      # from one wave to the next without CI noticing.
      #
      # The gate that DOES see that class is gates:type-check-spec — it runs
      # `tsc -p <project>/tsconfig.spec.json` over every project with a spec
      # config against a per-project baseline. It existed already, but only in
      # ci-full.yml, which fires weekly/on tags. Measured cost across 29
      # projects: ~165s. That is affordable per-PR, and it is the difference
      # between catching spec drift in one PR versus up to a week later.
      - name: Run type check (changed-file guard plus strict spec baseline)
        run: |
          BASE_REF="${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.base_sha }}"
          HEAD_REF="${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.head_sha }}"

          npm run gates:type-check-spec

        env:
          NX_DAEMON: 'false'
          NX_NO_CLOUD: 'true'
          NODE_OPTIONS: '--max-old-space-size=4096'

  test:
    needs: [install, detect-changes]
    if: >-
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true' &&
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' ||
       (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'))
    # pull-requests: read — a merge group carries no PR body; the entity-diff
    # witness reads its waiver from the queued pull request (see the step
    # "Resolve the queued pull request's body").
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Raised from 40 to 45 when the integration lane joined this job
    # (FARM-MEDIUM-301). The ceiling catches a runaway; it does not pace the
    # steps, and it is deliberately NOT their sum — the step budgets already add
    # to 140 minutes and always have, because target filtering means only a
    # subset of them does real work on any one PR. Each step carries its own
    # timeout so the STEP names the failure and the job ceiling is the backstop.
    #
    # 45 is not an arbitrary round number: ci-full's unfiltered `test` job
    # carries 45 (measured — median 23m29s, max 29m03s), and
    # tests/invariants/ci-timeout-budget-ssot.spec.ts requires the unfiltered
    # lane's budget to be at least this filtered one's. A filtered lane that may

name: CI - Affected

# ARCH-CI-005: Replaced global npm run scripts with nx affected commands
# SEC-CI-002: All third-party actions pinned to full commit SHAs
# ARCH-CI-006: Removed github.sha from NX cache key
# ARCH-CI-007: Split lint/type-check/test into parallel jobs so build always runs
# ARCH-CI-008: Increased timeouts (cold cache), reduced parallel (memory), save Nx cache after build
# ARCH-CI-009: Push-to-main runs affected lint/type-check/test/build as code-health.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # The merge queue (main ruleset) builds each group's merge commit and asks
  # for the same required checks; a workflow that does not listen here
  # leaves every queued entry waiting until the queue's timeout.
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]

# SEC-CI-021: Minimum token permissions — prevents compromised actions from
# pushing commits, creating releases, or modifying repository settings.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  NODE_VERSION: '22'
  NPM_CONFIG_CACHE: .npm-cache
  SENS_API_GATEWAY_CI_FEATURES: health,telemetry,metrics,strict-security,scada-display,lorawan,signed-deploy,tpm,st-bytecode,multi-task-scheduler,opc-ua-server,live-debug,license-enforce

jobs:
  detect-changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      base_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
      dependency_audit_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.dependency_audit_required }}
      docs_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.docs_changed }}
      farm_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.farm_checks_required }}
      full_validation: ${{ steps.range.outputs.full_validation }}
      has_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.has_changes }}
      deploy_changes: ${{ steps.check.outputs.deploy_changes }}
      head_sha: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
      infra_image_changed: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_infra }}
      infra_matrix: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.infra_matrix }}
      is_pr: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' }}
      range_reason: ${{ steps.range.outputs.range_reason }}
      rust_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.rust_checks_required }}
      selection_reason: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.selection_reason }}
      sensor_checks_required: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.sensor_checks_required }}
      validation_started_epoch: ${{ steps.range.outputs.validation_started_epoch }}
    steps:
      # SEC-CI-002: pinned to SHA
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Resolve immutable affected range
        id: range
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "validation_started_epoch=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if git ls-remote --exit-code --refs origin refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null; then
              git fetch --force --no-tags origin \
                '+refs/tags/deployed/development:refs/tags/deployed/development'
            else
              lookup_status=$?
              if [ "$lookup_status" -ne 2 ]; then
                echo "::error::Unable to resolve the development deployment baseline from origin."
                exit "$lookup_status"
              fi
              if git rev-parse --verify refs/tags/deployed/development >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                git tag --delete deployed/development
              fi
            fi
          fi
          node scripts/ci/resolve-affected-range.ts \
            --event-name "${{ github.event_name }}" \
            --ref "${{ github.ref }}" \
            --pr-base-sha "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}" \
            --head-sha "${{ github.sha }}" \
            --development-ref deployed/development

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm

      - name: Install workspace graph dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --prefer-offline

      - name: Resolve Nx and catalog scope
        id: scope
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.base_sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ steps.range.outputs.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/ci/select-deployment-scope.ts \
            --repo "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" \
            --base-sha "$BASE_SHA" \
            --head-sha "$HEAD_SHA" \
            --requested-services auto \
            --channel development
      - id: check
        env:
          DEPLOY_CHANGES: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.has_images }}
          VALIDATION_REQUIRED: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.validation_required }}
        run: |
          echo "has_changes=$VALIDATION_REQUIRED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "deploy_changes=$DEPLOY_CHANGES" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Shared setup: install + cache (reusable via needs + cache restore)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  install:
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Cache Nx
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .nx/cache
          key: nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
          restore-keys: |
            nx-ci-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit

      # Persist node_modules for downstream jobs
      - name: Cache node_modules
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: nm-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Lint, type-check, test: PR + push-to-main code-health gate
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  lint:
    needs: [install, detect-changes]
    if: >-
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true' &&
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group' ||
       (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      redis:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
      nats:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nats:2.10-alpine
        ports:
          - 4222:4222
          - 8222:8222
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "nats-server --version"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 10s
          --health-retries 10
    timeout-minutes: 40
    # continue-on-error removed: lint failures must block PR merge.
    # BEFORE: lint errors showed green in GitHub — no signal to reviewers or authors.

pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

  "agent_request_anchor": {
    "_doc": "ORPHAN-MEDIUM-492 \u2014 how long a minted agent-invocation request stays claimable. target_sha names the commit the request's plan and evidence are grounded at; past this window the request describes a tree the repo has moved off. The nightly cadence is daily and a request is meant to be consumed by the cycle that minted it, so 3 days is already generous. Age is the check that binds on the live lane: it needs no git history, so it works on the depth-1 shallow clone actions/checkout gives both ARIA workflows. Reachability is checked ONLY when an anchor is present AND the clone is not shallow (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-494) \u2014 in a partial clone, absence of the object is not evidence the commit is gone.",
    "max_age_seconds": 259200
  },
  "auto_promote": {
    "_doc": "Plan ARIA-V6 \u00a72e v2 \u2014 narrow auto-promotion exception. Default disabled; operator MUST opt-in via override. Even when enabled, the operator_approval path is UNCHANGED \u2014 auto-promote is a parallel admission, not a replacement.",
    "enabled": false,
    "min_clean_cycles": 5,
    "min_precision": 0.95,
    "profiles": [
      "autonomous"
    ]
  },
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "_doc": "ORPHAN-MEDIUM-483 / RC-4 \u2014 failure_window_hours is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. It is derived as minimum_window_hours(failure_threshold) = threshold x cadence + cadence, so for threshold 3 on the nightly's 24h cadence the window is 96. This file used to ship the literal 72, which is exactly the boundary the derivation exists to forbid: failures land at t=0/24/48 and the gate reads at t=72, so a 72h window puts the oldest failure on the edge and \u00b130min of cron jitter flips the verdict. Worse, the loader silently widened 72 to 96, so this file documented a number the code refused to honour and an operator reading it learned the wrong thing about their own breaker. Setting the key here again, or below the floor in an override, is now REFUSED with both numbers named rather than silently corrected.",
    "auto_downgrade_to": "strict",
    "failure_threshold": 3
  },
  "convergent_authoring": {
    "_doc": "Plan ARIA-V6 \u00a72d v2 \u2014 convergent adapter authoring loop config. Operator opt-in via skill-genesis request --convergent.",
    "max_authoring_rounds": 6,
    "max_rounds_override_enabled": false,
    "recall_floor": 0.9,
    "sandbox_min_fixtures": 10
  },
  "cost_caps_usd": {
    "daily": 5.0,
    "monthly": 100.0,
    "per_run": 0.5
  },
  "drift_class_weights": {
    "_doc": "Plan S4 (ORPHAN-MEDIUM-298) - per-drift-class pressure score multipliers. 1.0 = neutral (default behaviour is bit-identical); >1.0 biases cycles toward that class, <1.0 deprioritizes. Applied in pressure.run_pressure AFTER base scoring, re-capped at 100. Override via <repo>/aria-config/genesis_policy.json.",
    "adapter_shadow": 1.0,
    "belief_decay": 1.0,
    "contradiction": 1.0,
    "discovery": 1.0,
    "evidence_decay": 1.0,
    "process_health": 1.0,
    "runtime_signal": 1.0,
    "schema_drift": 1.0,
    "tool_governance": 1.0
  },
  "enable_request_generation": true,
  "f_finding_loop_guards": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-260 / ADR-0003 prerequisites 3-5 \u2014 loop guards on the aging F_FINDING plan source, which plans ARIA's own findings unattended. max_plans_per_24h: at most this many F_FINDING-sourced plans may START in any rolling 24h window, counted from plan_started stamps on the plan ledger (a plan an operator request bound never counts; 0 switches the source off; above 24 is REFUSED). cool_off_days: a finding whose earlier plan failed (implementation_rejected, plan_abandoned, plan_evaluated HUMAN_REQUIRED), or after whose merge another finding was emitted on the surfaces it changed, is not re-planned by this source for this many days; a plan the self-revert producer attributed a bad outcome to quarantines its finding until an operator-sourced plan for it starts. Operator requests (priority 0) are never judged by these guards. Read by finding_grounding.f_finding_loop_policy, key by key over this block; a block that is not an object, an unknown key or an out-of-bounds value refuses every F_FINDING candidate by name.",
    "cool_off_days": 7,
    "max_plans_per_24h": 1
  },
  "fitness_staleness_threshold_days": 7,
  "genesis_lifecycle": {
    "_doc": "Enterprise autonomy lifecycle gate. Skill/agent genesis cannot jump from pressure gap to request/draft/materialization without HUMAN_REQUIRED, real sandbox, SHADOW, EVAL_WINDOW and ACTIVE evidence.",
    "existing_capability_coverage_threshold": 0.8,
    "max_bridge_permanent_failures": 0,
    "max_critical_false_positives": 0,
    "max_noncritical_false_positives_30d": 3,
    "max_result_rejection_rate": 0.05,
    "min_evidence_refs": 3,
    "min_precision": 0.95,
    "min_recall": 0.9,
    "pressure_min_score": 70,
    "real_sandbox_min_fixture_results": 3,
    "real_sandbox_required_lanes": [
      "real_repo_baseline",
      "semantic_regression",
      "scope_violation_guard"
    ],
    "request_approval_mode": "panel",
    "shadow_min_clean_cycles": 5,
    "shadow_min_days": 14,
    "shadow_min_eval_runs": 10
  },
  "genesis_panel": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_panel_opens_per_cycle": 4
  },
  "implementer_turn_budget": {
    "_doc": "Operator decision 2026-09-16 (120; 2026-09-12 set 60, which the first live implementation spent to the turn before its commit) \u2014 budgeted Edit + Write + Bash + MultiEdit + NotebookEdit turns one implementer request may be admitted (cycle_and_turn_budget_cap, policy \u00a714). This was the literal 10 in turn_budget.IMPLEMENTER_TURN_BUDGET; each Edit is one turn and each test run is one Bash turn, so a root-cause implementation spends 20-40 and 10 was a wall. The cap exists to stop a runaway loop (perf CRIT-001 / ai HIGH-013); the run's job deadline is the real budget under the managed-subscription policy. Every reader takes the value from the policy of the workspace the tools store is bound to (turn_budget_policy.implementer_turn_budget_for_store): the executor compiles it into the spawn settings (--turn-budget), the hook admits each turn against it, and pre-merge refuses evidence recorded under any other cap by name. Values below 1 are REFUSED (a cap of zero refuses the first turn: that switches implementers off, it does not budget them); values above 2 x plan_convergence.MAX_AFFECTED_PATHS (400) are REFUSED with both numbers named so a policy cannot switch the cap off; a block that is not an object, or a key other than budgeted_turns (keys starting with _ are annotations), is REFUSED by name so a misspelling never silently runs on this default.",
    "budgeted_turns": 120
  },
  "judgment_pipeline": {
    "max_pending_per_role": 32,
    "sample_size_per_tool": 5
  },
  "materialization_requires_acknowledge": true,
  "max_requests_per_cycle": 5,
  "request_admission": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-364 (2026-10-07) \u2014 agent-request admission (request_admission.admit_request). Critical-path mints (plan steps, implementation and its reviews, operator acts) are always admitted. A discretionary mint is admitted only while the executor drains (no result or claim for executor_liveness_hours while a claimable request has waited as long stops it), the role has a provider that is not cooled, and the claimable backlog stays within budget = max(backlog_floor, backlog_days_of_drain x drained-per-day over drain_window_days). plan_seeds_per_cycle new plans start per cycle ahead of the budget (still requiring a draining executor and an uncooled provider), because panels and judges run earlier in the cycle and would otherwise take all headroom. An out-of-bounds value takes the shipped default and is disclosed once on governance (request_admission_policy_invalid). Measured 2026-10-06: ~28 drained/day against ~66 minted. Bounds: request_drain_capacity.REQUEST_ADMISSION_BOUNDS; a value outside them is refused by name.",

    "backlog_floor": 32,
    "drain_window_days": 7,
    "executor_liveness_hours": 36.0,
    "plan_seeds_per_cycle": 1
  },

purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

{
  "$schema": "aria/genesis-policy/v1",
  "agent_request_anchor": {
    "_doc": "ORPHAN-MEDIUM-492 \u2014 how long a minted agent-invocation request stays claimable. target_sha names the commit the request's plan and evidence are grounded at; past this window the request describes a tree the repo has moved off. The nightly cadence is daily and a request is meant to be consumed by the cycle that minted it, so 3 days is already generous. Age is the check that binds on the live lane: it needs no git history, so it works on the depth-1 shallow clone actions/checkout gives both ARIA workflows. Reachability is checked ONLY when an anchor is present AND the clone is not shallow (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-494) \u2014 in a partial clone, absence of the object is not evidence the commit is gone.",
    "max_age_seconds": 259200
  },
  "auto_promote": {
    "_doc": "Plan ARIA-V6 \u00a72e v2 \u2014 narrow auto-promotion exception. Default disabled; operator MUST opt-in via override. Even when enabled, the operator_approval path is UNCHANGED \u2014 auto-promote is a parallel admission, not a replacement.",
    "enabled": false,
    "min_clean_cycles": 5,
    "min_precision": 0.95,
    "profiles": [
      "autonomous"
    ]
  },
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "_doc": "ORPHAN-MEDIUM-483 / RC-4 \u2014 failure_window_hours is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. It is derived as minimum_window_hours(failure_threshold) = threshold x cadence + cadence, so for threshold 3 on the nightly's 24h cadence the window is 96. This file used to ship the literal 72, which is exactly the boundary the derivation exists to forbid: failures land at t=0/24/48 and the gate reads at t=72, so a 72h window puts the oldest failure on the edge and \u00b130min of cron jitter flips the verdict. Worse, the loader silently widened 72 to 96, so this file documented a number the code refused to honour and an operator reading it learned the wrong thing about their own breaker. Setting the key here again, or below the floor in an override, is now REFUSED with both numbers named rather than silently corrected.",
    "auto_downgrade_to": "strict",
    "failure_threshold": 3
  },
  "convergent_authoring": {
    "_doc": "Plan ARIA-V6 \u00a72d v2 \u2014 convergent adapter authoring loop config. Operator opt-in via skill-genesis request --convergent.",
    "max_authoring_rounds": 6,
    "max_rounds_override_enabled": false,
    "recall_floor": 0.9,
    "sandbox_min_fixtures": 10
  },
  "cost_caps_usd": {
    "daily": 5.0,
    "monthly": 100.0,
    "per_run": 0.5
  },
  "drift_class_weights": {
    "_doc": "Plan S4 (ORPHAN-MEDIUM-298) - per-drift-class pressure score multipliers. 1.0 = neutral (default behaviour is bit-identical); >1.0 biases cycles toward that class, <1.0 deprioritizes. Applied in pressure.run_pressure AFTER base scoring, re-capped at 100. Override via <repo>/aria-config/genesis_policy.json.",
    "adapter_shadow": 1.0,
    "belief_decay": 1.0,
    "contradiction": 1.0,
    "discovery": 1.0,
    "evidence_decay": 1.0,
    "process_health": 1.0,
    "runtime_signal": 1.0,
    "schema_drift": 1.0,
    "tool_governance": 1.0
  },
  "enable_request_generation": true,
  "f_finding_loop_guards": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-260 / ADR-0003 prerequisites 3-5 \u2014 loop guards on the aging F_FINDING plan source, which plans ARIA's own findings unattended. max_plans_per_24h: at most this many F_FINDING-sourced plans may START in any rolling 24h window, counted from plan_started stamps on the plan ledger (a plan an operator request bound never counts; 0 switches the source off; above 24 is REFUSED). cool_off_days: a finding whose earlier plan failed (implementation_rejected, plan_abandoned, plan_evaluated HUMAN_REQUIRED), or after whose merge another finding was emitted on the surfaces it changed, is not re-planned by this source for this many days; a plan the self-revert producer attributed a bad outcome to quarantines its finding until an operator-sourced plan for it starts. Operator requests (priority 0) are never judged by these guards. Read by finding_grounding.f_finding_loop_policy, key by key over this block; a block that is not an object, an unknown key or an out-of-bounds value refuses every F_FINDING candidate by name.",
    "cool_off_days": 7,
    "max_plans_per_24h": 1
  },
  "fitness_staleness_threshold_days": 7,
  "genesis_lifecycle": {
    "_doc": "Enterprise autonomy lifecycle gate. Skill/agent genesis cannot jump from pressure gap to request/draft/materialization without HUMAN_REQUIRED, real sandbox, SHADOW, EVAL_WINDOW and ACTIVE evidence.",
    "existing_capability_coverage_threshold": 0.8,
    "max_bridge_permanent_failures": 0,
    "max_critical_false_positives": 0,
    "max_noncritical_false_positives_30d": 3,
    "max_result_rejection_rate": 0.05,
    "min_evidence_refs": 3,
    "min_precision": 0.95,
    "min_recall": 0.9,
    "pressure_min_score": 70,
    "real_sandbox_min_fixture_results": 3,
    "real_sandbox_required_lanes": [
      "real_repo_baseline",
      "semantic_regression",
      "scope_violation_guard"
    ],
    "request_approval_mode": "panel",
    "shadow_min_clean_cycles": 5,
    "shadow_min_days": 14,
    "shadow_min_eval_runs": 10
  },
  "genesis_panel": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_panel_opens_per_cycle": 4
  },
  "implementer_turn_budget": {
    "_doc": "Operator decision 2026-09-16 (120; 2026-09-12 set 60, which the first live implementation spent to the turn before its commit) \u2014 budgeted Edit + Write + Bash + MultiEdit + NotebookEdit turns one implementer request may be admitted (cycle_and_turn_budget_cap, policy \u00a714). This was the literal 10 in turn_budget.IMPLEMENTER_TURN_BUDGET; each Edit is one turn and each test run is one Bash turn, so a root-cause implementation spends 20-40 and 10 was a wall. The cap exists to stop a runaway loop (perf CRIT-001 / ai HIGH-013); the run's job deadline is the real budget under the managed-subscription policy. Every reader takes the value from the policy of the workspace the tools store is bound to (turn_budget_policy.implementer_turn_budget_for_store): the executor compiles it into the spawn settings (--turn-budget), the hook admits each turn against it, and pre-merge refuses evidence recorded under any other cap by name. Values below 1 are REFUSED (a cap of zero refuses the first turn: that switches implementers off, it does not budget them); values above 2 x plan_convergence.MAX_AFFECTED_PATHS (400) are REFUSED with both numbers named so a policy cannot switch the cap off; a block that is not an object, or a key other than budgeted_turns (keys starting with _ are annotations), is REFUSED by name so a misspelling never silently runs on this default.",
    "budgeted_turns": 120
  },
  "judgment_pipeline": {
    "max_pending_per_role": 32,
    "sample_size_per_tool": 5
  },
  "materialization_requires_acknowledge": true,
  "max_requests_per_cycle": 5,
  "request_admission": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-364 (2026-10-07) \u2014 agent-request admission (request_admission.admit_request). Critical-path mints (plan steps, implementation and its reviews, operator acts) are always admitted. A discretionary mint is admitted only while the executor drains (no result or claim for executor_liveness_hours while a claimable request has waited as long stops it), the role has a provider that is not cooled, and the claimable backlog stays within budget = max(backlog_floor, backlog_days_of_drain x drained-per-day over drain_window_days). plan_seeds_per_cycle new plans start per cycle ahead of the budget (still requiring a draining executor and an uncooled provider), because panels and judges run earlier in the cycle and would otherwise take all headroom. An out-of-bounds value takes the shipped default and is disclosed once on governance (request_admission_policy_invalid). Measured 2026-10-06: ~28 drained/day against ~66 minted. Bounds: request_drain_capacity.REQUEST_ADMISSION_BOUNDS; a value outside them is refused by name.",
    "backlog_days_of_drain": 2.0,
    "backlog_floor": 32,
    "drain_window_days": 7,
    "executor_liveness_hours": 36.0,
    "plan_seeds_per_cycle": 1
  },

purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

{
  "$schema": "aria/auto-action-policy/v1",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "comment": "Plan ARIA-V3 §A0 + §2a — single source of truth for the L3 exclusion list (kernel-immutability + auth/tenant/migrations/infra/secrets/billing/production). Consumed by lane_classifier diff classifier (materialize-time) AND auto_merge.evaluate_auto_merge (merge-time). Adding/removing entries requires an ADR per Plan ARIA-V3 §B3.",
  "l3_lane_exclusion_globs": [
    "aria-kernel/**",
    "apps/auth-service/**",
    "**/auth/**",
    "**/tenant/**",
    "**/tenant-context/**",
    "**/tenant-isolation/**",
    "**/migrations/**",
    "**/database/migrations/**",
    "**/migration-runner/**",
    ".github/workflows/**",
    "infrastructure/**",
    "platform/**",
    ".env*",
    "**/secrets/**",
    "**/credentials/**",
    "apps/billing-service/**",
    "**/billing/**",
    "**/production/**",
    "docker-compose*.yml",
    "Dockerfile*",
    "**/k8s/**",
    "**/helm/**",
    "**/argocd/**",
    "**/terraform/**"
  ],
  "l3_lane_exclusion_reason_codes": {
    "aria-kernel/**": "kernel_immutability",
    "apps/auth-service/**": "auth_surface",
    "**/auth/**": "auth_surface",
    "**/tenant/**": "tenant_isolation_surface",
    "**/tenant-context/**": "tenant_isolation_surface",
    "**/tenant-isolation/**": "tenant_isolation_surface",
    "**/migrations/**": "schema_migration_surface",
    "**/database/migrations/**": "schema_migration_surface",
    "**/migration-runner/**": "schema_migration_surface",
    ".github/workflows/**": "ci_supply_chain_surface",
    "infrastructure/**": "infra_surface",
    "platform/**": "platform_surface",
    ".env*": "secrets_surface",
    "**/secrets/**": "secrets_surface",
    "**/credentials/**": "secrets_surface",
    "apps/billing-service/**": "billing_surface",
    "**/billing/**": "billing_surface",
    "**/production/**": "production_surface",
    "docker-compose*.yml": "deploy_surface",
    "Dockerfile*": "deploy_surface",
    "**/k8s/**": "deploy_surface",
    "**/helm/**": "deploy_surface",
    "**/argocd/**": "deploy_surface",
    "**/terraform/**": "infra_surface"
  },
  "_doc_note": "Glob patterns use fnmatch semantics with '/' separators. The classifier resolves each candidate path via Path.resolve() (worktree-aware, follows symlinks) BEFORE matching to prevent path-evasion attacks (e.g. .worktrees/snowball/aria-kernel/foo would be normalized to /abs/aria-kernel/foo and matched). Adding a glob: (a) add it to l3_lane_exclusion_globs, (b) add the matching reason_code key, (c) update I-V3-29 parametrization. Removing a glob: requires ADR per Plan ARIA-V3 §B3 + SPEC §0.2 review."
}

  "comment": "Plan ARIA-V3 §A0 + §2a — single source of truth for the L3 exclusion list (kernel-immutability + auth/tenant/migrations/infra/secrets/billing/production). Consumed by lane_classifier diff classifier (materialize-time) AND auto_merge.evaluate_auto_merge (merge-time). Adding/removing entries requires an ADR per Plan ARIA-V3 §B3.",
  "l3_lane_exclusion_globs": [
    "aria-kernel/**",
    "apps/auth-service/**",
    "**/auth/**",
    "**/tenant/**",

  ],
  "l3_lane_exclusion_reason_codes": {
    "aria-kernel/**": "kernel_immutability",
    "apps/auth-service/**": "auth_surface",
    "**/auth/**": "auth_surface",
    "**/tenant/**": "tenant_isolation_surface",

    "**/helm/**": "deploy_surface",
    "**/argocd/**": "deploy_surface",

  "_doc_note": "Glob patterns use fnmatch semantics with '/' separators. The classifier resolves each candidate path via Path.resolve() (worktree-aware, follows symlinks) BEFORE matching to prevent path-evasion attacks (e.g. .worktrees/snowball/aria-kernel/foo would be normalized to /abs/aria-kernel/foo and matched). }

purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

{
  "$schema": "aria/genesis-policy/v1",
  "agent_request_anchor": {
    "_doc": "ORPHAN-MEDIUM-492 \u2014 how long a minted agent-invocation request stays claimable. target_sha names the commit the request's plan and evidence are grounded at; past this window the request describes a tree the repo has moved off. The nightly cadence is daily and a request is meant to be consumed by the cycle that minted it, so 3 days is already generous. Age is the check that binds on the live lane: it needs no git history, so it works on the depth-1 shallow clone actions/checkout gives both ARIA workflows. Reachability is checked ONLY when an anchor is present AND the clone is not shallow (ORPHAN-CRITICAL-494) \u2014 in a partial clone, absence of the object is not evidence the commit is gone.",
    "max_age_seconds": 259200
  },
  "auto_promote": {
    "_doc": "Plan ARIA-V6 \u00a72e v2 \u2014 narrow auto-promotion exception. Default disabled; operator MUST opt-in via override. Even when enabled, the operator_approval path is UNCHANGED \u2014 auto-promote is a parallel admission, not a replacement.",
    "enabled": false,
    "min_clean_cycles": 5,
    "min_precision": 0.95,
    "profiles": [
      "autonomous"
    ]
  },
  "circuit_breaker": {
    "_doc": "ORPHAN-MEDIUM-483 / RC-4 \u2014 failure_window_hours is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. It is derived as minimum_window_hours(failure_threshold) = threshold x cadence + cadence, so for threshold 3 on the nightly's 24h cadence the window is 96. This file used to ship the literal 72, which is exactly the boundary the derivation exists to forbid: failures land at t=0/24/48 and the gate reads at t=72, so a 72h window puts the oldest failure on the edge and \u00b130min of cron jitter flips the verdict. Worse, the loader silently widened 72 to 96, so this file documented a number the code refused to honour and an operator reading it learned the wrong thing about their own breaker. Setting the key here again, or below the floor in an override, is now REFUSED with both numbers named rather than silently corrected.",
    "auto_downgrade_to": "strict",
    "failure_threshold": 3
  },
  "convergent_authoring": {
    "_doc": "Plan ARIA-V6 \u00a72d v2 \u2014 convergent adapter authoring loop config. Operator opt-in via skill-genesis request --convergent.",
    "max_authoring_rounds": 6,
    "max_rounds_override_enabled": false,
    "recall_floor": 0.9,
    "sandbox_min_fixtures": 10
  },
  "cost_caps_usd": {
    "daily": 5.0,
    "monthly": 100.0,
    "per_run": 0.5
  },
  "drift_class_weights": {
    "_doc": "Plan S4 (ORPHAN-MEDIUM-298) - per-drift-class pressure score multipliers. 1.0 = neutral (default behaviour is bit-identical); >1.0 biases cycles toward that class, <1.0 deprioritizes. Applied in pressure.run_pressure AFTER base scoring, re-capped at 100. Override via <repo>/aria-config/genesis_policy.json.",
    "adapter_shadow": 1.0,
    "belief_decay": 1.0,
    "contradiction": 1.0,
    "discovery": 1.0,
    "evidence_decay": 1.0,
    "process_health": 1.0,
    "runtime_signal": 1.0,
    "schema_drift": 1.0,
    "tool_governance": 1.0
  },
  "enable_request_generation": true,
  "f_finding_loop_guards": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-260 / ADR-0003 prerequisites 3-5 \u2014 loop guards on the aging F_FINDING plan source, which plans ARIA's own findings unattended. max_plans_per_24h: at most this many F_FINDING-sourced plans may START in any rolling 24h window, counted from plan_started stamps on the plan ledger (a plan an operator request bound never counts; 0 switches the source off; above 24 is REFUSED). cool_off_days: a finding whose earlier plan failed (implementation_rejected, plan_abandoned, plan_evaluated HUMAN_REQUIRED), or after whose merge another finding was emitted on the surfaces it changed, is not re-planned by this source for this many days; a plan the self-revert producer attributed a bad outcome to quarantines its finding until an operator-sourced plan for it starts. Operator requests (priority 0) are never judged by these guards. Read by finding_grounding.f_finding_loop_policy, key by key over this block; a block that is not an object, an unknown key or an out-of-bounds value refuses every F_FINDING candidate by name.",
    "cool_off_days": 7,
    "max_plans_per_24h": 1
  },
  "fitness_staleness_threshold_days": 7,
  "genesis_lifecycle": {
    "_doc": "Enterprise autonomy lifecycle gate. Skill/agent genesis cannot jump from pressure gap to request/draft/materialization without HUMAN_REQUIRED, real sandbox, SHADOW, EVAL_WINDOW and ACTIVE evidence.",
    "existing_capability_coverage_threshold": 0.8,
    "max_bridge_permanent_failures": 0,
    "max_critical_false_positives": 0,
    "max_noncritical_false_positives_30d": 3,
    "max_result_rejection_rate": 0.05,
    "min_evidence_refs": 3,
    "min_precision": 0.95,
    "min_recall": 0.9,
    "pressure_min_score": 70,
    "real_sandbox_min_fixture_results": 3,
    "real_sandbox_required_lanes": [
      "real_repo_baseline",
      "semantic_regression",
      "scope_violation_guard"
    ],
    "request_approval_mode": "panel",
    "shadow_min_clean_cycles": 5,
    "shadow_min_days": 14,
    "shadow_min_eval_runs": 10
  },
  "genesis_panel": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_panel_opens_per_cycle": 4
  },
  "implementer_turn_budget": {
    "_doc": "Operator decision 2026-09-16 (120; 2026-09-12 set 60, which the first live implementation spent to the turn before its commit) \u2014 budgeted Edit + Write + Bash + MultiEdit + NotebookEdit turns one implementer request may be admitted (cycle_and_turn_budget_cap, policy \u00a714). This was the literal 10 in turn_budget.IMPLEMENTER_TURN_BUDGET; each Edit is one turn and each test run is one Bash turn, so a root-cause implementation spends 20-40 and 10 was a wall. The cap exists to stop a runaway loop (perf CRIT-001 / ai HIGH-013); the run's job deadline is the real budget under the managed-subscription policy. Every reader takes the value from the policy of the workspace the tools store is bound to (turn_budget_policy.implementer_turn_budget_for_store): the executor compiles it into the spawn settings (--turn-budget), the hook admits each turn against it, and pre-merge refuses evidence recorded under any other cap by name. Values below 1 are REFUSED (a cap of zero refuses the first turn: that switches implementers off, it does not budget them); values above 2 x plan_convergence.MAX_AFFECTED_PATHS (400) are REFUSED with both numbers named so a policy cannot switch the cap off; a block that is not an object, or a key other than budgeted_turns (keys starting with _ are annotations), is REFUSED by name so a misspelling never silently runs on this default.",
    "budgeted_turns": 120
  },
  "judgment_pipeline": {
    "max_pending_per_role": 32,
    "sample_size_per_tool": 5
  },
  "materialization_requires_acknowledge": true,
  "max_requests_per_cycle": 5,
  "request_admission": {
    "_doc": "ARIA-HIGH-364 (2026-10-07) \u2014 agent-request admission (request_admission.admit_request). Critical-path mints (plan steps, implementation and its reviews, operator acts) are always admitted. A discretionary mint is admitted only while the executor drains (no result or claim for executor_liveness_hours while a claimable request has waited as long stops it), the role has a provider that is not cooled, and the claimable backlog stays within budget = max(backlog_floor, backlog_days_of_drain x drained-per-day over drain_window_days). plan_seeds_per_cycle new plans start per cycle ahead of the budget (still requiring a draining executor and an uncooled provider), because panels and judges run earlier in the cycle and would otherwise take all headroom. purpose.text:
The learned conventions that touch any of ``paths`` — latest row per
pattern_id, confidence ≥ ``min_confidence``, strongest first, capped.

This is the read that puts the conventions ledger into production:
``record_convention`` has written a row on every converged cycle since
V9.0-F, and until the mint-time envelope enrichment (Plan "ARIA Sinir
Sistemi" FAZ 4) nothing ever read one back. Same verified-chain
discipline as ``lookup_pattern``: a quarantined ledger yields nothing
rather than something unverifiable.

`base_dir` is keyword-REQUIRED (no default) on purpose: a summary that
cannot open the store cannot honestly claim anything about artifact
integrity, and a default would let a caller silently produce that claim.

# File-Upload Virus-Scan Contract Specification

> **Status:** OPEN — design specification only. The implementation
> requires an operational decision on daemon hosting (sidecar / managed
> service / disabled) that this document does NOT make. The contract
> below is the architecturally fixed surface that any chosen implementation
> will plug into.
>
> **Closes (when implemented):** Phase 6.2.2 of the farm-module plan
>
> **Related:** `libs/storage/src/file-upload-security.service.ts:25-30`
> (the existing service's docblock that names the deferred surfaces)

## Why this contract exists

`FileUploadSecurityService` already lands four of six Phase 6.2 surfaces:

  - max file size enforcement (per-document-type + global cap)
  - mime whitelist (per-document-type)
  - magic-byte sniff fallback
  - **EXIF strip** for image uploads (sharp-based, fail-safe)

The two that remain — **ClamAV virus scan** and **orphan cleanup cron** —
diverge in nature: orphan cleanup is already shipped (`StorageOrphanCleanupService`).
That leaves virus scan as the last unwired Phase 6.2 surface.

The implementation is gated on an operational decision (where does the
clamd daemon run? sidecar? managed service?) that an autonomous loop
cannot make. But the **contract** between
`FileUploadSecurityService` and any virus-scan implementation IS
definable, and definable now would let the implementing PR plug in
without re-deriving the integration shape from scratch.

## What this contract specifies

### 1. The `VirusScanProvider` interface

Every implementation (ClamAV, VirusTotal, AWS Macie, no-op for dev)
satisfies this single interface:

```typescript
// libs/storage/src/virus-scan/virus-scan-provider.ts
export interface ScanResult {
  /** True when the scanner did NOT find any signatures. */
  isClean: boolean;
  /** Threat name when isClean=false; null when clean OR scan failed open. */
  threat: string | null;
  /** When the scan completed. */
  scannedAt: Date;
  /**
   * The scanner that produced this result. Lets consumers correlate
   * "this row was scanned by clamd vs that row by VirusTotal" when
   * the implementation changes mid-life.
   */
  scannerName: string;
  /**
   * Scan duration. Operational metric for watchdog dashboards
   * (slow scans → daemon overload signal).
   */
  durationMs: number;
}

export interface VirusScanProvider {
  /**
   * Scan a buffer. Implementations:
   * - MUST return isClean=true OR isClean=false; never throw on a
   *   clean result.
   * - MAY throw on transport errors (daemon unreachable, timeout).
   *   Callers handle the throw via the post-upload async pattern
   *   below — a transport error does NOT block the upload.
   * - MUST be idempotent — same buffer twice returns the same
   *   result.
   * - MUST complete within the configured timeout
   *   (default 30s). The provider is responsible for honouring
   *   timeouts; callers do NOT wrap with their own.
   */
  scan(buffer: Buffer, contentType: string): Promise<ScanResult>;

  /**
   * Health-check for the scanner. Returns true when the scanner is
   * reachable and ready. Used by `/health/ready` to decide whether
   * uploads should proceed (degraded mode: accept upload, mark
   * isInfected=null, scan later when scanner returns).
   */
  isReady(): Promise<boolean>;
}
```

### 2. The async post-upload integration

`FileUploadSecurityService.uploadSecure()` extends with a NON-BLOCKING
post-upload step:

```
preflight → strip EXIF → minio.uploadFile → return UploadResult
                                          ↓
                                          schedules async scan

# File-Upload Virus-Scan Contract Specification

> **Status:** OPEN — design specification only. The implementation
> requires an operational decision on daemon hosting (sidecar / managed
> service / disabled) that this document does NOT make. The contract
> below is the architecturally fixed surface that any chosen implementation
> will plug into.
>
> **Closes (when implemented):** Phase 6.2.2 of the farm-module plan
>
> **Related:** `libs/storage/src/file-upload-security.service.ts:25-30`
> (the existing service's docblock that names the deferred surfaces)

## Why this contract exists

`FileUploadSecurityService` already lands four of six Phase 6.2 surfaces:

  - max file size enforcement (per-document-type + global cap)
  - mime whitelist (per-document-type)
  - magic-byte sniff fallback
  - **EXIF strip** for image uploads (sharp-based, fail-safe)

The two that remain — **ClamAV virus scan** and **orphan cleanup cron** —
diverge in nature: orphan cleanup is already shipped (`StorageOrphanCleanupService`).
That leaves virus scan as the last unwired Phase 6.2 surface.

The implementation is gated on an operational decision (where does the
clamd daemon run? sidecar? managed service?) that an autonomous loop
cannot make. But the **contract** between
`FileUploadSecurityService` and any virus-scan implementation IS
definable, and definable now would let the implementing PR plug in
without re-deriving the integration shape from scratch.

## What this contract specifies

### 1. The `VirusScanProvider` interface

Every implementation (ClamAV, VirusTotal, AWS Macie, no-op for dev)
satisfies this single interface:

```typescript
// libs/storage/src/virus-scan/virus-scan-provider.ts
export interface ScanResult {
  /** True when the scanner did NOT find any signatures. */
  isClean: boolean;
  /** Threat name when isClean=false; null when clean OR scan failed open. */
  threat: string | null;
  /** When the scan completed. */
  scannedAt: Date;
  /**
   * The scanner that produced this result. Lets consumers correlate
   * "this row was scanned by clamd vs that row by VirusTotal" when
   * the implementation changes mid-life.
   */
  scannerName: string;
  /**
   * Scan duration. Operational metric for watchdog dashboards
   * (slow scans → daemon overload signal).
   */
  durationMs: number;
}

export interface VirusScanProvider {
  /**
   * Scan a buffer. Implementations:
   * - MUST return isClean=true OR isClean=false; never throw on a
   *   clean result.
   * - MAY throw on transport errors (daemon unreachable, timeout).
   *   Callers handle the throw via the post-upload async pattern
   *   below — a transport error does NOT block the upload.
   * - MUST be idempotent — same buffer twice returns the same
   *   result.
   * - MUST complete within the configured timeout
   *   (default 30s). The provider is responsible for honouring
   *   timeouts; callers do NOT wrap with their own.
   */
  scan(buffer: Buffer, contentType: string): Promise<ScanResult>;

  /**
   * Health-check for the scanner. Returns true when the scanner is
   * reachable and ready. Used by `/health/ready` to decide whether
   * uploads should proceed (degraded mode: accept upload, mark
   * isInfected=null, scan later when scanner returns).
   */
  isReady(): Promise<boolean>;
}
```

post-upload step:
